ai.description: *Hemidactylus sushilduttai* is a small gecko (SVL ~45 mm) with a pale brown body and dark transverse bands. It is distinguished by a lack of enlarged tubercles and a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus sushilduttai* is best distinguished by the presence of 6–8 longitudinal rows of enlarged, strongly keeled tubercles that extend across its back.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus sushilduttai* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops and dry deciduous forests at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus sushilduttai* is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively hunt small insects on rocky surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus sushilduttai* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus sushilduttai* is endemic to the Mahendragiri hills in the Eastern Ghats of Odisha, India, occurring at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
